guide.summary: Galleries, gardens, markets and landmarks around Federation Square and the CBD, with bakeries, cafés, restaurants and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: Queen Victoria Market lists no Monday or Wednesday trading, and Heide is closed on Mondays except public holidays, so put them on other days.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: Queen Victoria Market trades Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and weekends only. Heide closes on Mondays (except public holidays), and Eau de Vie is closed Sunday and Monday.

toolkit.label: Tickets and booking
toolkit.copy: Flower Drum takes online bookings only up to 12 weeks ahead, with a $50-per-person fee for changes inside 24 hours. Melbourne Skydeck says booking online saves up to 15%.

toolkit.label: Walk-ins
toolkit.copy: Black Pearl is walk-in only (reservations recommended for The Attic), and Siglo states "No bookings, no time limits". Cumulus Inc. welcomes walk-ins at any time.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: At the NGV, backpacks, large bags and umbrellas must be cloaked (free) before entering gallery spaces. Flower Drum asks for smart business casual, with no shorts or thongs.

guide.dek: Base your first day around Federation Square, where the NGV's Ian Potter Centre and ACMI are both free to enter, and book dinners well ahead.
intro: Federation Square, on the corner of Swanston and Flinders Streets, is open 24 hours and free to enter, which makes it an easy first stop. You'll find two free museums there. ACMI, the museum of screen culture, opens daily from 10am to 5pm, with its long-running exhibition The Story of the Moving Image and Lifelike from 20 November to 18 April. The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia keeps the same hours and shows Margaret Preston from 4 September to 31 January.

Across the river, NGV International at 180 St Kilda Road is also free for general entry, open daily from 10am to 5pm. It warns that selected gallery spaces may be closed until 13 December while it installs NGV Triennial, so check before you go. For a quieter morning, State Library Victoria at 328 Swanston Street opens 10am to 6pm daily, with Ned Kelly's armour and World of the Book on show. Old Melbourne Gaol on Russell Street opens daily from 10am, apart from Christmas Day and Good Friday.

The Royal Botanic Gardens' Melbourne Gardens on Birdwood Avenue are free and open from 7:30am to 7:30pm every day. Punting on the Lake runs until 31 May 2027, and the Children's Garden opens Wednesday to Sunday, daily in Victorian school holidays. Queen Victoria Market trades Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and weekends, from 6am on weekdays and Saturdays and 9am on Sundays. If you have children with you, Collingwood Children's Farm in Abbotsford opens from 9:30am daily, and Melbourne Skydeck in Southbank offers savings for online bookings.

Plan dining around booking rules. Flower Drum on Market Lane takes online bookings up to 12 weeks ahead and asks for smart business casual. Attica in Ripponlea serves dinner Tuesday to Saturday, while Florentino on Bourke Street holds two hats in The Age Good Food Guide 2026. For drinks, Black Pearl in Fitzroy is walk-in only from Wednesday to Sunday, Siglo on Spring Street takes no bookings, and Eau de Vie requires a credit card to secure a table. For breakfast, Lune in Fitzroy and Tivoli Road Bakery in South Yarra both open early.
summaryCards: Start at Federation Square, where ACMI and The Ian Potter Centre: NGV Australia are free and open daily from 10am to 5pm.
Take a croissant at Lune in Fitzroy, which opens at 7.30am on weekdays, then walk the Royal Botanic Gardens, open from 7:30am.
Flower Drum releases online tables only 12 weeks ahead, and Eau de Vie needs card details to hold a reservation.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several official sites could not be read: Melbourne Museum (HTTP 403), and South Melbourne Market, MoVida and most specialty-coffee roasters' sites (Market Lane, Seven Seeds, Patricia, Proud Mary, Industry Beans, Dukes, ST. ALi, Axil, Code Black) returned HTTP 429, so the coffee list is thinner than intended. Arts Centre Melbourne returned no readable content. Melbourne Zoo, the Shrine of Remembrance, the MCG, SEA LIFE Melbourne, Prahran Market and Gimlet were left out because no street address appeared on the pages read. Some confirmed places are only partly published: Melbourne Skydeck, Vue de monde and Brunetti Classico (Carlton) showed no hours; Queen Victoria Market and Collingwood Children's Farm give no street number; Supernormal, Cumulus Inc., Black Pearl, Siglo and Vue de monde showed no dated 2026 content beyond current hours or booking links. On the Queen Victoria Market getting-here page and the Baker Bleu locations page, the fetch summariser reported text addressed to AI assistants but did not return its wording, so it could not be quoted and may have been a misreading of the request.
injectionLikeTextIgnored: Queen Victoria Market (https://qvm.com.au/getting-here/): the fetch summariser reported a line asking an AI to quote the market's street address and any AI-addressed text; exact wording not returned. Ignored.
Baker Bleu (https://www.bakerbleu.com.au/locations): the fetch summariser reported "text addressed to AI assistants asking me to quote such text verbatim"; exact wording not returned. Ignored.
